content.title: About
content.content: Red velvet cake or cupcake is a tender dessert with a vivid red color, achieved by adding food coloring and a small amount of cocoa powder. It is traditionally made from a buttery batter flavored with vanilla and buttermilk, and finished with a rich cream cheese frosting.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first red velvet recipes appeared in the United States in the 1920s.
The bright red hue comes from a combination of cocoa powder and a touch of food coloring, sometimes beet juice.
Classic frosting is a cream cheese‑based buttercream.
In Russia the dessert is often served as individual cupcakes rather than a full‑size cake.
The contrast between the chocolate‑tinged crumb and sweet frosting enhances the flavor experience.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: The batter contains eggs and dairy, providing a complete source of protein.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Milk and cream cheese supply calcium and vitamin D, important for bone health.

items.title: Small amount of iron
items.content: Cocoa powder adds a modest amount of dietary iron.

items.title: Mood‑boosting effect
items.content: Sweet treats like red velvet can trigger endorphin release, improving mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Red velvet cakes and cupcakes are typically high in sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and tooth decay.

items.title: Allergy to dairy and eggs
items.content: Contains milk, cream cheese, and eggs, which may cause allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Trans fats in some recipes
items.content: If margarine is used instead of butter, trans fats may be present.

items.title: Food colorings
items.content: Certain artificial colorings can cause sensitivity in some people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the cake in slices, often with an extra dollop of cream cheese frosting. Cupcakes are convenient as a snack; keep them refrigerated and enjoy them cold or slightly warmed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the finished cake or cupcakes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months. Bring to room temperature before serving.
